answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making reputation expensive: newcomers start in an open meadow of untrusted identities and must earn attestations from established peers through completed, paid transactions. Each voucher spends time and copper tokens, so faking one identity is cheap but faking a thousand is not. The attestation graph also exposes fraud: a cluster of accounts whose endorsements all trace back to a single umber thread of self-dealing stands out, and peers simply refuse to trade with it.
